title: Dispatch queue TOP (50): the row goal walks the whole date index
prompt: Warehouse dispatch screen: about 200 terminals poll, 6 calls per second in total. Average 2.8 s, CPU-bound, and
slower every week. Actual plan: ordered forward scan of IX_Orders_OrderDate with residual Status = 'Pending', then a
Key Lookup to PK_Orders for ShipRegionID and a Filter. The scan was estimated to read about 200k rows (row goal) and
read about 29.9M. Statistics are current (FULLSCAN last night): the estimate for Status = 'Pending' alone is right
(about 60k). All Pending orders are from the last 72 hours, so the oldest-first scan reads almost the whole index
before the first match. 'Pending' is always a literal in this statement; @RegionID comes from the terminal.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
baseline_sql: SELECT TOP (50) o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

correct_families.description: The statement stays the same; OrderID is added to ORDER BY so that ties at the 50th row are deterministic. This is allowed and optional.
reference_sql: SELECT TOP (50) o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

correct_families.description: Fallback when an index cannot be added: turn the row goal off so the optimizer seeks the 60k Pending rows and sorts them.
reference_sql: SELECT TOP (50) o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

traps.why: The per-column estimates are already right. Histograms cannot express that Pending rows sit only at the newest end.
The row-goal estimate is the same on every compile.
example_sql: SELECT TOP (50) o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

traps.why: A parameter in place of the literal 'Pending' can no longer match a filtered index.
example_sql: SELECT TOP (50) o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

traps.why: WITH TIES returns more than 50 rows when orders share the 50th OrderDate.
traps.told_apart_by: Sixty Pending orders of one region with the same batch OrderDate.
example_sql: SELECT TOP (50) WITH TIES o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

traps.why: A hint on IX_Orders_Status is brittle and still needs about 60k lookups and a sort on every call.
example_sql: SELECT TOP (50) o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

min_improvement.basis: The scan reads about 29.9M rows per call. A seek in OrderDate order stops after 50 rows.

key.reference_notes: Before a filtered index is created, every session that modifies Orders must use the SET options that filtered indexes require.
